Arnold Alois Schwarzenegger[c] (born July 30, 1947) is an Austrian and American actor, businessman, film producer, former politician, and former professional bodybuilder who served as the 38th governor of California from 2003 to 2011.[5] He is recognized as a cultural icon acting in numerous action films which have grossed over $5.4 billion worldwide.[6] His accolades include a Primetime Emmy Award and a Golden Globe Award. He received a Motion Picture Star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1984.

Schwarzenegger began lifting weights at the age of 15 and won Mr. Universe at the age of 20, and the Mr. Olympia title seven times.[d] Nicknamed the "Austrian Oak" in his bodybuilding days, he is regarded as one of the greatest bodybuilders of all time.[7][8] He wrote the autobiographical Arnold: The Education of a Bodybuilder (1977) and appeared in the bodybuilding documentary Pumping Iron (1977).[9]

After retiring from bodybuilding, Schwarzenegger gained worldwide fame as a Hollywood action star starring as the title role in Conan the Barbarian (1982), and its sequel, Conan the Destroyer (1984) and as Terminator in The Terminator franchise (1984–2019).[10][11] He also acted in the action films Commando (1985), The Running Man (1987), Predator (1987), Total Recall (1990), True Lies (1994), and Batman & Robin (1997) as well as the comedies Twins (1988), Kindergarten Cop (1990), Last Action Hero (1993) and Jingle All the Way (1996).[12]

As a registered member of the Republican Party, Schwarzenegger chaired the President's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports during most of the George H. W. Bush administration. In 2003, he was elected governor of California in a special recall election, and later ran again where he was reelected in the 2006 gubernatorial election.[e][13] In 2011, he reached his term limit as governor and returned to acting.

After a hiatus, he returned to action films starring in The Expendables films (2010–2014), Escape Plan (2013), and Maggie (2015). On television, he starred in the Netflix docu-series Arnold (2023), and action comedy series FUBAR (2023–2025). He also has written seven books including his memoir Total Recall: My Unbelievably True Life Story (2012) and is the founder of the film production company Oak Productions.[14]

Early life and education

Arnold Alois Schwarzenegger was born on July 30, 1947, in Thal, Styria,[15] the second son of Gustav Schwarzenegger and his wife, Aurelia (née Jadrny; 1922–1998). Gustav was the local chief of police and, after the Anschluss in 1938, joined the Nazi Party and in 1939 the Sturmabteilung (SA). During World War II, Gustav served as a military policeman in the invasions of Poland, France, and the Soviet Union, including the siege of Leningrad, rising to the rank of hauptfeldwebel.[16][17] He was wounded in the summer of 1942 at Leningrad, later contracted malaria, and was discharged from the Heer in February 1944. He returned to service with the Ordnungspolizei as a Preisüberwachungsbeamter ("price control official") in Mürzzuschlag, Austria, and did not resume civilian law-enforcement duties until 1947.[18][19]

According to Holocaust scholar Michael Berenbaum, Gustav served "in theaters of the war where atrocities were committed. But there is no way to know from the documents whether he played a role."[16] Gustav's background received wide press attention during the 2003 California gubernatorial recall election in which Schwarzenegger was elected.[20]

Gustav married Aurelia on October 20, 1945; he was 38 and she was 23. According to Schwarzenegger, his parents were very strict: "Back then in Austria it was a very different world ... if we did something bad or we disobeyed our parents, the rod was not spared."[21] He was raised in a Catholic household.[22] Gustav favored his elder son, Meinhard, over Arnold.[23] His favoritism was "strong and blatant", stemming from an unfounded suspicion that Arnold was not his biological child.[24] Schwarzenegger has said that his earliest childhood memory is climbing into his parents' bed during a thunderstorm and lying between them.[25] He has also said that his father had "no patience for listening or understanding your problems".[22] He maintained a close relationship with his mother and stayed in contact with her until her death.[26]

In a 2004 interview with Fortune, Schwarzenegger said he suffered what "would now be called child abuse" at the hands of his father: "My hair was pulled. I was hit with belts. So was the kid next door. It was just the way it was. Many of the children I've seen were broken by their parents, which was the German-Austrian mentality. They didn't want to create an individual. It was all about conforming. I was one who did not conform, and whose will could not be broken. Therefore, I became a rebel. Every time I got hit, and every time someone said, 'You can't do this,' I said, 'This is not going to be for much longer because I'm going to move out of here. I want to be rich. I want to be somebody.'"[17]
